checks.requirement: Verify the precise approximation topology and witness quantifiers
checks.finding: PaperSmoothApproximation existentially chooses one sequence of smooth data and classical solutions, with data converging in H^gamma and flows converging uniformly on [0,T] in L2. It does not require convergence of every sequence, a numerical convergence rate, uniform-in-data approximation speed, or H^gamma smoothness of the rough datum beyond its stated membership. The target p.11 uses precisely the canonical cutoff witnesses and uniform solution-L2 passage. Although p.11 only needs L2 data convergence and an H^gamma bound, its chosen cutoffs also converge in H^gamma, and that stronger witness property is actually proved by cutoff_converges. Thus it does not remove the selected flow.

checks.requirement: Show the certificate is available for every source-selected admissible datum
checks.finding: positive_kdv_flow_exists constructs the original-source continuous flow for every real mean-zero positive-Sobolev datum. exact_solution_exists and kdv_solution_smooth_approximation supply its actual cutoff-based certificate. The latter chooses data=cutoff m f, proves H^gamma convergence, constructs smooth flows for every m, and derives uniform-in-time L2 convergence from exact-flow dependence. No certificate, data ball, or stability estimate is imported as an extra premise. Hence the certificate is an available witness for every selected flow, rather than an extra restriction on target data or solutions.

checks.requirement: Verify classical approximants against actual PDE and smoothness
checks.finding: PaperSmoothSolution requires initial trace, continuous spatial regularity of all Sobolev orders, smooth time coefficients, the differentiated actual PDE on the interior, and reality/zero mean. These are requirements on the smooth approximants, not on the rough target datum or flow. The existing all_regular_coefficient_contDiffOn derives endpoint time regularity for the constructed smooth flows. classical_to_duhamel proves variation of constants from the classical PDE; paperSmooth_iff_historical proves both directions. Thus the classical certificate is not merely a renamed Duhamel assumption, and it is available for the source cutoff construction.

checks.requirement: Identify the selected flow in both directions without admitting extra flows
checks.finding: paperApproximation_iff_historical is two-way for these actual witnesses. approximation_determines_flow identifies any continuous path with that certificate with the reference flow built from the same exact BIT inputs, at every time of [0,T]; the eventual L2 data bound is derived from convergence. paperSolution_iff_exactSolution proves both directions for the source-selected convention. Consequently allowing general smooth witnesses instead of only the canonical cutoffs neither adds distinct selected flows nor excludes the canonical one. Using approximation in this reverse direction is legitimate because selection by smooth approximation belongs to the target convention.
